Alexander Kirkpatrick, 37, Florida Hoxha, 34, Florin Hoxha, 36, and Eris Cani were killed Sept. 25 when a two-story building collapsed in Athens’ historic Plaka district.
The four Americans were among the six killed in the blast, believed to have been caused by a major gas leak, Athens Mayor Haris Doukas said.
Kirkpatrick and Florida Hoxha had married on Long Island the month before the blast and were ending their honeymoon in Athens, according to Newsday .
Florin Hoxha was the brother of the bride. Florin Hohxa accompanied the couple alongside his longtime partner, Cani, who was five months pregnant with their first child, according to media reports .

A 19 year-old Athens man who was a juvenile at the time of his 2024 arrest has been indicted this month by a Limestone County grand jury on separate single charges of manslaughter and murder.

Cedric Fuqua of Athens was indicted September 17 in connection with his alleged role in the death of Ladevine Adre Crutcher, 33, of Athens. Crutcher died in a shooting that occurred on September 7 of 2024 at the Fifth Avenue Apartment complex in north Athens. The apartment complex is operated by the City of Athens Housing Authority.
According to court documents, Fuqua is currently incarcerated without bond.

The dad of a British teenager brutally murdered by her husband in Greece has revealed her six-year-old daughter still doesn't know her own father killed her mum.

Helicopter pilot Babis Anagnostopoulos is serving a 27-year sentence in jail for murdering 19-year-old Caroline Crouch as she and their then-11-month-old daughter Lydia slept in their home in Athens in May 2021. Anagnostopoulos callously protested his innocence for more than a month, claiming robbers had broken into their home, killing the family dog, stealing €15,000 (£12,825) cash and €25,000 (£21,375) worth of jewellery, then suffocating Caroline.

His lies were eventually exposed after evidence on Caroline's Fitbit smartwatch refuted his story. Caroline’s dad David, 83, has a framed picture of his granddaughter on the wall of his home in Greece, where he has given a new interview from his bed.

Nearly a week after a woman’s dismembered body was found at a Smyrna apartment complex , police said Tuesday that an autopsy revealed she had been shot.

Shanteria Mosley, 25, was shot in the head before her remains were found across different days and different locations last week, Smyrna police said in a news release. Officials did not say whether the gunshot wound caused the victim’s death or if it occurred before or after she had been dismembered.
The 18-year-old accused in her death, Kingston Bradley, remains at the Cobb County jail on charges of murder and concealing the death of another.

article.title: Smyrna dismemberment case: Disbelief as murder probe continues
article.description: Smyrna police arrested 18-year-old Kingston Bradley after finding human remains at the Park Valley Apartments on Wednesday.
paragraphs: Smyrna police arrested 18-year-old Kingston Bradley after a witness spotted him carrying a plastic tub containing the torso of Katie Moseley at Park Valley Apartments.
SMYRNA, Ga. - Authorities are releasing new details regarding the timeline surrounding the murder of a woman at a Smyrna apartment complex last week.
Smyrna police say 18-year-old Kingston Bradley killed Shanteria "KT" Mosley between 10 a.m. and noon last Wednesday.

According to court documents, the investigation began as a missing person search at the Park Valley Apartments in Smyrna, where officers initially found nothing. Court documents state a witness later saw Bradley carrying a plastic tub through an open area of the complex. When Bradley realized someone had seen him, he dropped the tub onto a dirt path and ran to an apartment.
According to court documents, the plastic tub contained Mosley's torso. Police said they subsequently located additional remains inside a car trunk.

The United States Senate has blocked a resolution that would have required President Donald Trump’s administration to report on the killing of nine Americans in the occupied West Bank and on Israel’s treatment of Palestinian children in military detention.

article.title: Israeli Settlers Attack West Bank Village and Block Palestinian Family
paragraphs: More than 100 Israeli settlers have carried out attacks in a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank, stopping a family escorted by the Israeli military from returning to their homes, which had been seized weeks ago by settlers.

Two houses belonging to the al-Tubasi family in Jalud, south of Nablus, were set on fire in the raid on Monday night and Israeli security forces were also targeted by settlers. Human rights groups say the events show how Israeli authorities are failing to take effective action against settler violence.
"It was extremely terrifying, beyond words. It's hard to imagine the situation," Mahmoud al-Tubasi told the BBC.
"My feeling now is that I am happy to have escaped death. I genuinely expected they were going to kill us."

Al-Tubasi, 60, his wife Aida, 51, and their 33-year-old son, Wael, had returned to their properties accompanied by Israeli forces after Israel's High Court ruled earlier this month that they must be allowed to go back.

Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki said the Taibah electricity distribution station was targeted at 5.11am local time on Tuesday, September 29. The Civil Defence spokesperson said the ballistic missile had been launched by the Houthi militia towards residential areas. Debris from the interception damaged several buildings and vehicles. No casualties were reported.

In a statement on X, coalition spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Malki said two ballistic missiles were intercepted and destroyed over Khamis Mushait and Jazan, while four drones were intercepted and destroyed over Khamis Mushait.
Al-Maliki said the coalition would continue taking and implementing operational measures to deter the Houthi militia.
